stem: More than 90% of anogenital warts are caused by which low-risk HPV types?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Confuses cutaneous wart types with anogenital wart types.
options.explanation: HPV types 1 and 2 are cutaneous types that cause plantar and common warts on the hands and feet, not most anogenital warts.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Swaps the high-risk oncogenic types for the low-risk wart types.
options.explanation: HPV types 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types linked to cervical and anogenital cancers rather than to most genital warts.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None — HPV 6 and 11 cause more than 90% of anogenital warts.
options.explanation: CDC: more than 90% of cases of anogenital warts are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 or 11.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes any common genital HPV genotype causes warts, ignoring risk class.
options.explanation: HPV types 31 and 33 are additional high-risk types associated with cervical precancer and cancer, not the typical genital wart.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Confuses anogenital warts with epidermodysplasia verruciformis types.
options.explanation: HPV types 5 and 8 are linked to epidermodysplasia verruciformis and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, not anogenital warts.

context: Learning objective: Low-risk HPV types 6 or 11 cause more than 90% of cases of anogenital warts.
